_help: ONE CALL PER FILE. Copy this file into storm-content/calls/<category>/<id>.json and fill it in. Every key starting with _ is a note for humans and is ignored by the game. Delete the notes or leave them, both are fine.
name: Name of call as the player sees it
category: rtc | fire | medical | police | rescue | hazmat
_category: which service family the call belongs to. Drives the scoring (was the player's keyword in the right family) and which colour/pin style it gets.
_domain: land = roads, buildings, open ground. water = river, canal, lake, coastline, harbour (suggestion draws from lifeboats, coastguard, fire boat, marine police; coastguard helicopter desk available). air = airports/aircraft. The location types below must belong to the same domain.
_weight: base chance of this call spawning compared with every other enabled call. 1 = normal, 3 = three times as common, 0.2 = rare, 0 = never (use enabled:false instead).

weightBy._help: OPTIONAL multipliers on top of weight. Each matching entry multiplies the base weight; anything missing means no change. Delete this whole block for a plain call.
weightBy._hour: 24h ranges 'start-end' (inclusive). Rush hour RTCs, night-time domestics, that kind of thing.
weightBy._weather: the game's own simple weather state; only these seven keys exist.
weightBy._areaType: what kind of area the spawn point sits in, worked out from the map around it.
weightBy._coverage: multiplier per service the player currently has crewed stations for; a call needing a service the player has none of should be 0 for that service.

_grade: TRUE urgency, 1 (most urgent) to 4. The player's own priority pick is scored against this. Grade 1 = life at risk now, 2 = emergency, 3 = urgent, 4 = routine.
_responseMinutes: units must be on scene within this many minutes or the call counts as late.
_onSceneMinutes: how long the units stay on scene, min and max, picked at random.
_reward: Response Points on a clean resolution, scaled by the interrogation score.
_locationTypes: HARD RULE: the call can only spawn at a real place of one of these types (an RTC only on roads, a domestic only at house/flats, a boat only on water). Pick from the list below.

_locationTypesAvailable._note: new types can be added in the locations content file (key, label, category, domain); once added there they can be used here.

units._help: the predetermined attendance: what the game SUGGESTS when the player picks this call's keyword. Keys are vehicle type keys from the vehicles content file (irv, rpt, single_pump, dual_pump, aerial, rescue_unit, otl, fire_officer, rrv, hart, hems, arv, npas, dog_unit, lifeboat_all_weather, lifeboat_inshore, coastguard_rescue_team, cg_helicopter, fire_boat ... add more in vehicles.json). Anything not listed is not suggested. Ambulances are NOT listed here, they come from patients below.

patients._range: minimum and maximum number of patients; one ambulance is suggested per patient. [0, 0] for a call with no patients.
patients._rrvChance: out of 100, chance a Rapid Response Vehicle is added on top of the ambulances.
patients._conditions: pool the patients' conditions are drawn from; shows in the Patients section and the UKHS record.

desks._help: automatic desk reviews that run when the call is classified. The player cannot request these. chance is out of 100; a desk that triggers self-tasks its unit after delaySeconds and logs an event, otherwise it logs 'not required'. Delete any desk that never applies.

escalations._help: OPTIONAL mid-incident messages from the crews once on scene (fire make-ups, extra casualties found). afterSeconds is measured from the first unit arriving. Use [] for none.

openings: First thing the caller says when the handler presses Call Start, one is picked at random
caller._phoneArea: auto = a number local to the spawn location; or 'mobile'; or 'withheld'.
caller._callerType: witness | patient | relative | staff | alarm_company | police_officer ... only affects the caller-ID text and how the answers read.

dialogue._help: the caller's answers to each interrogation button, in the order the player can press them. Button ids are fixed: start, callerName, patientName, address, whatHappened, conscious, breathing, pain, bleeding, medicalHistory, medications, patientAge, reassure, refer111. Give at least one answer per button; one is picked at random each time it is pressed. Placeholders: {{address}} {{callerName}} {{patients}} {{firstPatientName}}. Exactly ONE button must have revealsAddress:true. Buttons with diagnostic:true count towards the interrogation score.
